messages:
sasha: FYI discovered CVE-2026-1234 in our SSL dependency (libssl wrapper used by the serving runtime). Affects hosted API and Dedicated pools that haven't been rebuilt with the patched matrix. Private installs notified separately.
rajiv: do we have exploit PoC in the wild?
emily: no confirmed PoC yet, there's a public writeup but no working exploit. CVSS 8.1, remote exploitable if TLS renegotiation is exposed.
rajiv: ok that reduces immediate public exposure but still high severity. Any customers on Dedicated running older images?
leah: I pulled inventory: ~40 Dedicated clusters running runtimes with libssl <=1.2.7 patch-level X. High-tier customers (Enterprise & Committed) are on newer images, mid-market has the larger surface.
mike: Hosted API uses autoscaling pools; we can do rolling deploys but need rollout policy to avoid latency SLO hits. Suggest canary then ramp.
sasha: proposed plan: 1) Hosted: emergency rolling deploy with canary (10%) then 30m observation window, full rollout within 48h. 2) Dedicated: schedule reserved time windows, prioritize enterprise SLAs first. 3) Private: notify customers with CV and remediation steps.
emily: agree. Also enable extra audit logging for TLS handshakes for 72h to detect anomalous renegotiation attempts. We can tie logs to existing audit pipeline.
rajiv: oncall note: add temporary WAF rule to drop suspicious renegotiation sequences where possible. That buys time for non-patched Dedicated clusters.
oncall-bot: created ticket SEC-2026-488 in Jira: "CVE-2026-1234 mitigation and rollout" assigned to @rajiv, priority P1, due in 48h. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2026-488
leah: customer comms: draft that we need 60-90 minute maintenance window for Dedicated clusters; prefer 02:00-04:00 PT. Should we give 72h notice for non-enterprise?
mike: enterprise customers need a heads-up ASAP. For mid-market, standard 72h. Hosted: we can deploy in <48h without scheduled downtime but call it a short degraded window in case of rollback.
sasha: rollback plan: snapshot runtime images pre-rollout, keep fallback model variants and regional capacity. If latency regressions >10% we rollback canary and pause rollout.
emily: quick check command for ops: `openssl version -a` and `ldd /opt/runtime/bin/llm_serving | grep ssl` — include in runbook.
rajiv: who can own the Hosted deploy? I can take first shift, @mike will own Dedicated scheduling and customer comms with @leah.
mike: ack. I'll prepare calendar invites and comms template, will post to #announcements and notify account reps.
sasha: final decision: Hosted emergency rolling deploy starting within 4 hours; Dedicated prioritized by customer tier with maintenance windows over next 72 hours; Private customers get advisory and patch artifacts immediately.
emily: add postmortem checklist item to evaluate any missed detections and update dependency pinning policy (block unpinned transitive deps).
leah: I'll draft the customer advisory and include instructions for KMS key checks (KMS not affected but note rotation cadence).
oncall-bot: SEC-2026-488 status updated: in progress.
sasha: thanks team. I'll own the post-deploy validation (latency/cost/err rates) and close the ticket when green. :thumbsup:
